channel.title: SecuBuzz · Cybersecurity News Briefs
channel.description: Fast, factual 60-word cybersecurity briefs and CISA KEV alerts for security professionals.

item.title: ISACA Updates COBIT 7 with AI Risk Scenarios
item.description: ISACA released COBIT 7, the latest version of its governance framework, adding AI risk scenarios. The update provides comprehensive guidance, a digital platform, and customizable resources to help organizations manage emerging AI risks. Security teams should review the new scenarios and integrate them into their governance and risk management processes.

item.title: Red Hat Releases MySQL 8.4 Security Update
item.description: Red Hat issued a security update for the mysql:8.4 module on Red Enterprise Linux 9.8 Extended Update Support. The update addresses multiple vulnerabilities, each with a CVSS base score listed in the CVE references, but no active exploitation has been reported. Administrators should apply the RHSA-2026:102188 update promptly to mitigate potential exploitation of the identified flaws.

item.title: Red Hat Releases Kernel Update for RHEL 10
item.description: Red Hat released a kernel update for Red Enterprise Linux 10 to address multiple security bugs. The update contains fixes for several kernel vulnerabilities, each with a CVSS base score listed in the CVE references, but no active exploitation has been reported. Administrators should apply the RHSA-2026:102168 update promptly to mitigate potential exploitation of the identified flaws.

item.title: Fence-Agents Receives Important Security Update
item.description: Red Hat released an Important security update for the fence-agents package on RHEL 8. The update addresses multiple vulnerabilities that could allow privilege escalation or denial of service, as indicated by the CVSS scores linked in the advisory. Administrators should apply the fence-agents update immediately and verify that the affected services are restarted to enforce the new security controls.

item.title: Matilda Sells Claimed VMware vCenter Exploit
item.description: A forum seller named Matilda is offering a claimed exploit for VMware vCenter Server, targeting CVE-2026-123890. The critical vulnerability would let an attacker create a new vCenter administrator account, but no confirmed exploitation has been reported. Broadcom issued a patch on November 19, 2026; administrators should apply it immediately to mitigate the risk.

item.title: Curl Receives Moderate Security Update
item.description: Red Hat issued a Moderate security update for the curl package on RHEL 8. The patch fixes several vulnerabilities that could lead to remote code execution or information disclosure, as reflected in the CVSS scores. System administrators should install the curl update promptly and restart any services that depend on it to apply the security fixes.

item.title: Red Hat Releases Kernel Security Update for RHEL6
item.description: A kernel vulnerability affecting Red Hat Enterprise Linux 6 Extended Lifecycle Support prompted an Important security update. The flaw, detailed in multiple CVE references, carries a CVSS base score indicating significant risk, but no active exploitation has been reported. Red Hat has released the patch; administrators should apply the update immediately to mitigate potential exploitation.

item.title: Red Hat Issues Thunderbird Security Update
item.description: An Important security update for Thunderbird on Red Hat Enterprise Linux 8 addresses a kernel-level vulnerability. The vulnerability, referenced by multiple CVE entries, has a CVSS base score reflecting high risk, though no active exploitation has been observed. Red Hat has issued the patch; users are advised to install it promptly to prevent potential compromise.

item.title: Red Hat Updates libgsf for Security
item.description: Red Hat released a security update for libgsf on RHEL 10.2 EUS, addressing multiple vulnerabilities identified by CVE references. The flaws involve improper handling of GSF files, potentially allowing remote code execution via crafted documents. Red Hat has issued a patch; administrators should apply the update immediately to mitigate exploitation.

item.title: git-lfs Security Update for Red Hat Enterprise Linux 10
item.description: Red Hat released a security update for git-lfs on Red Hat Enterprise Linux 10, addressing a vulnerability that could allow code execution. The flaw, referenced by multiple CVEs, permits attackers to inject malicious content during file transfer operations, potentially compromising system integrity. Red Hat recommends applying the latest git-lfs package immediately to mitigate the risk, with no additional workarounds required.

item.title: QEMU KVM MA Flaw Allows Local Privilege Escalation
item.description: Red Enterprise Linux 7 Extended Lifecycle Support users face a qemu-kvm-ma flaw that may enable local privilege escalation via the virtual machine monitor. The vulnerability stems from improper memory mapping handling, and Red Hat rates it Moderate with a CVSS base score in the CVE references. Apply the qemu-kvm-ma update immediately; no workaround exists until the patch is installed.

item.title: GNOME Remote Desktop Vulnerability Enables Remote Code Execution
item.description: Red Enterprise Linux 9.8 Extended Update Support users face a gnome-remote-desktop flaw that permits remote code execution via the remote desktop protocol. The issue arises from unchecked input during session negotiation, and Red Hat rates it Important with a CVSS base score in the CVE references. Apply the gnome-remote-desktop update immediately; no workaround exists until the patch is installed.

item.title: Red Hat Issues Security Update for xdg-desktop-portal
item.description: Red Hat released a security update for the xdg-desktop-portal component in Red Enterprise Linux 10, addressing multiple vulnerabilities. The update mitigates flaws that could allow privilege escalation or unauthorized data access, with CVSS scores provided in the CVE references. Administrators should apply the RHSA-2026:102177 update immediately to ensure protection against the identified weaknesses.

item.title: Volkswagen Cars Exposed via Bluetooth Spy Flaws
item.description: Researchers demonstrated that Bluetooth flaws in Volkswagen vehicles enable eavesdropping on conversations and GPS tracking. The flaws grant unauthorized cabin control and location access, exposing private data and enabling remote manipulation, with a 16-month exposure after disclosure. Volkswagen should expedite the release of a patch and advise owners to disable Bluetooth or apply the fix immediately to mitigate the risk.

item.title: OpenAI Finds Zero-Day Mobile OS Bypass and RCE
item.description: OpenAI’s GPT-6.2 Astra discovered zero-day flaws in a popular mobile OS and a common network service. The flaws include a permission-bypass exposing private data and a remote code execution path reachable from a low-privileged role. No vendor patch is yet available; security teams should monitor OpenAI advisories and apply any future OS or service updates promptly.

item.title: Red Hat Updates mingw-expat for RHEL8
item.description: Red Hat released an Important security update for mingw-expat on Red Hat Enterprise Linux 8 to fix a kernel-related flaw. The flaw, cited in several CVE references, carries a CVSS base score indicating high severity, but no active exploitation has been reported. The vendor has made the patch available; administrators should apply it immediately to mitigate potential exploitation.

item.title: Cleverbridge Reports Card Data Theft
item.description: Cleverbridge confirmed that attackers exfiltrated payment card data from its e-commerce platform, including card numbers, expiration dates, and CVV codes. The breach involved unauthorized access to the platform’s database, exposing sensitive payment information to malicious actors. Cleverbridge has begun notifying affected customers and is investigating the incident; affected users should monitor accounts for fraudulent activity.

item.title: Red Hat Updates librabbitmq on RHEL 8
item.description: Red Hat issued a security update for librabbitmq on RHEL 8, addressing vulnerabilities rated as Important. The vulnerabilities lack a publicly disclosed CVE identifier in the advisory, but Red Hat provides CVSS base scores for each through referenced CVE links. Security teams should apply the librabbitmq update immediately to mitigate the identified risks.

item.title: Red Hat Updates libgsf on RHEL 9
item.description: Red Hat released a security update for libgsf on RHEL 9, addressing vulnerabilities rated as Important. No specific CVE identifiers are listed in the advisory, but CVSS base scores are available via referenced CVE links for each vulnerability. Apply the libgsf update promptly to reduce exposure to the identified weaknesses.

item.title: Red Hat gfs2-utils security update released
item.description: Red Hat released a gfs2-utils update for Enterprise Linux 9, fixing a flaw that could allow arbitrary code via malformed GFS2 metadata. The issue stems from improper handling of GFS2 superblock fields, with a CVSS base score indicating moderate impact; no active exploitation observed. Apply the patch through the standard update channel to mitigate the risk.

item.title: Red Hat libgsf security update released
item.description: Red Hat released a libgsf update for Enterprise Linux 9.8 EUS, fixing a flaw that could allow arbitrary code via malformed GSF files. The issue stems from insufficient validation of GSF headers, with a CVSS base score indicating important impact; no active exploitation reported. Apply the patch via the standard update channel to mitigate the risk.

item.title: Red Hat Releases xdg-desktop-portal Security Update
item.description: Red Hat released a security update for xdg-desktop-portal on RHEL 9.2 Update Services for SAP Solutions, fixing multiple vulnerabilities. The update is rated Important, with CVSS base scores for each flaw listed via CVE links in the references, indicating moderate-to-high risk. Red Hat advises applying the patch immediately; no work-arounds are available, and users should confirm installation through update channels.

item.title: ISC Stormcast: Monday November 23, 2026
item.description: The SANS Internet Storm Center releases its weekly Stormcast podcast for Monday, November 23, 2026. The episode covers current threat landscape insights, emerging attack trends, and defensive best practices shared by industry experts. Listeners can access the recording and transcript via the ISC website, providing a resource for security teams to stay informed.

item.title: Red Hat Updates flatpak on RHEL 8.8
item.description: Red Hat released a security update for flatpak on RHEL 8.8, addressing vulnerabilities rated as Important. The advisory does not list specific CVE identifiers, but CVSS base scores are provided via referenced CVE links for each vulnerability. Security teams should apply the flatpak update promptly to mitigate the identified risks.

item.title: Red Hat Issues Important libgsf Security Update
item.description: Red Hat released a libgsf update on RHEL 10, fixing vulnerabilities that could enable local privilege escalation or denial of service. The advisory lists CVSS base scores and references CVE identifiers, though specific CVE numbers are omitted. Red Hat recommends applying the update immediately via the RPM package or system update tools to mitigate exploitation risk.

item.title: Red Hat Flatpak Update Fixes Security Vulnerabilities
item.description: Red Hat issued a flatpak patch for RHEL 8.4 to fix multiple security flaws. The update addresses privilege-escalation and information-leak vulnerabilities, each with a CVSS score listed via CVE references, but no exploitation reported. Apply the flatpak update immediately; no workaround exists, and users should confirm the new flatpak version post-install.

item.title: Red Hat Kernel Patch Addresses Multiple Security Flaws
item.description: Red Hat issued a kernel patch for RHEL 10.2 EUS to fix multiple Linux kernel security flaws. The update addresses privilege-escalation and information-leak flaws, each with a CVSS score listed via CVE references, but no active exploitation has been seen. Red Hat advises applying the kernel update immediately; no workaround exists, and users should confirm the new kernel version post-install.

item.title: Red Hat Issues fltk Security Patch
item.description: Red Enterprise Linux 9 users receive an important security update for the fltk GUI toolkit. The update addresses one or more vulnerabilities that could allow attackers to execute code or compromise system integrity, as indicated by the CVSS base score linked in the advisory. Red Hat recommends applying the patch immediately to mitigate the risk.

item.title: Google Blocks AI Tool Calls with Governance
item.description: Google introduces semantic governance policies on its Gemini platform, allowing enterprises to pre-screen AI agent tool calls. The policies evaluate each proposed tool invocation against user intent and company rules, blocking non-compliant actions at the Agent Gateway enforcement point. Organizations can configure permissions to define allowed actions, enhancing control over AI agent behavior.

item.title: Red Hat Updates python-oauthlib Security
item.description: Red Enterprise Linux 8.8 users receive an important security update for python-oauthlib, a library used for OAuth authentication. The update fixes one or more vulnerabilities that could enable attackers to bypass authentication or inject malicious tokens, as indicated by the CVSS base score referenced in the advisory. Red Hat advises applying the patch promptly to secure authentication flows.

item.title: Red Hat python-oauthlib Patch Resolves Security Issues
item.description: Red Hat released a python-oauthlib patch for RHEL 8.4 to address several security vulnerabilities. The update mitigates privilege-escalation and information-leak flaws, each assigned a CVSS score and referenced via CVE links, with no active exploitation observed. Apply the python-oauthlib update immediately; no workaround is available, and users should verify the new package version after installation.

item.title: Red Hat Releases Open vSwitch 2.15 Security Update
item.description: Red Hat released a security update for Open vSwitch 2.15 on RHEL 8 Fast Datapath, addressing a vulnerability that could allow unauthorized traffic manipulation. The advisory rates the issue as Important, with CVSS base scores linked to CVE entries, indicating a high-severity flaw that may enable remote code execution.

item.title: Red Hat Releases openvswitch 3.6 Patch
item.description: Red Enterprise Linux 10 users receive an important security update for openvswitch 3.6, a software switch used in virtual networking. The update addresses one or more vulnerabilities that could allow attackers to execute code or disrupt network traffic, as indicated by the CVSS base score linked in the advisory. Red Hat recommends applying the patch immediately to protect virtual networks.

item.title: Debian 13.8 Bundles Kernel and Chromium Fixes
item.description: Debian 13.8 bundles security fixes for the kernel, Chromium, Firefox ESR, OpenJDK 25, nginx, BIND 9, Dovecot, rsync, PostgreSQL 17, and 112 other packages. The update covers 122 advisories, DSA-6408 to DSA-6629, fixing critical bugs that could enable privilege escalation. Users should run 'apt update && apt upgrade' on trixie, verify packages, and monitor Debian Security Advisories for further patches.

item.title: GL.iNet Cloud Flaw Enables Router and KVM Malware
item.description: Hackers leveraged a flaw in GL.iNet’s cloud-based remote-management service to compromise customer routers and KVM devices. The vulnerability permits unauthenticated code execution, enabling attackers to drop custom malware, establish backdoors, and spawn reverse shells for persistent remote control. GL.iNet has released a patch for the cloud service; administrators should apply the update immediately and verify device firmware integrity.

item.title: Debian, Ubuntu Remove rsyslogd Timestamp Config Directive
item.description: Debian and Ubuntu removed a configuration directive from rsyslogd in early 2023, changing syslog timestamp handling. The change removes a legacy option that allowed custom timestamp formatting, potentially causing logs to default to system time zones and reducing forensic precision. Users should review rsyslogd configuration files for timestamp settings and apply any vendor updates that reintroduce desired formatting options.

item.title: VirusTotal Detects Ransomware Missed by 75 AV Engines
item.description: VirusTotal introduced a runtime encryption check that identified a Python ransomware sample previously undetected by 75 antivirus engines. The malware leveraged obfuscated Python code to evade static signatures, but its encryption activity triggered the new behavior analysis, revealing its malicious intent. Security teams should enable VirusTotal’s behavior-based detection and ensure their antivirus solutions are updated to recognize similar obfuscated ransomware.

item.title: Cleverbridge Reports Credit Card Data Theft
item.description: Cleverbridge, an e-commerce platform, disclosed a breach that exposed customers’ payment card numbers and CVV codes via unauthorized system access. The intrusion involved credential theft and data exfiltration, potentially enabling fraud, but no public exploit or CVE was identified. Cleverbridge urged affected users to monitor accounts, change passwords, and contact issuers while investigating the vector and will issue remediation guidance.

item.title: Optimizely Malware Hits 178 Organizations
item.description: An attacker exploited a flaw in Optimizely’s web experimentation platform to plant malicious JavaScript on 178 organizations’ websites, such as BBC, CNN, and Zoom. The vulnerability, a memory-corruption flaw in OpenJDK’s Base64 decoder (CVE-2026-114938), requires specific CPU conditions, limiting exploitation but still high severity. Optimizely confirmed the incident, urged customers to update the platform, remove injected scripts, and monitor traffic.

item.title: OpenRouter Removes Providers After Prompt Theft Discovery
item.description: OpenRouter removed three AI inference providers after researchers uncovered months of prompt theft from their internal systems. The stolen prompts, some marked Zero Data Retention, were accessed without authorization, exposing user inputs; Dragos confirmed the breach to vendors. OpenRouter recommends vendors review access controls, enforce strict data-retention policies, and apply security hardening to prevent future prompt exfiltration.

item.title: Ghostscript Sandbox Escape RCE Demonstrated via File Uploads
item.description: Researchers demonstrated a sandbox-escape RCE flaw in Ghostscript, a common PDF/PostScript interpreter on Linux servers, via crafted file uploads. The flaw lets attackers bypass Ghostscript’s isolation and run arbitrary commands on the host, compromising the web application; a PoC was released by pwn.ai. Ghostscript issued a patch; admins should apply it immediately and verify file-upload handling remains sandboxed.

item.title: OpenRouter Removes Compromised AI Hosts, Revokes Zero Data Retention
item.description: OpenRouter removed three AI hosting providers and revoked Zero Data Retention for 125 endpoints after detecting provider compromise. The flaw arises from third-party providers lacking secure isolation, risking private chat data leakage; no breach confirmed, but exposure persists. OpenRouter notified affected customers, removed compromised providers, and revoked Zero Data Retention; teams should verify endpoint settings and monitor anomalous access.

item.title: Red Hat Issues Critical PHP Patch for RHEL7
item.description: Red Hat released a critical PHP update for RHEL7 Extended Lifecycle Support, fixing high-severity vulnerabilities that could allow remote code execution. The patch covers several CVE-identified flaws, each rated with a CVSS base score indicating critical impact, though no exploitation has been seen. Apply the update immediately via RHSA-2026:101337 to keep PHP secure.

item.title: Ghostscript Upload2Shell Enables Remote Command Execution
item.description: Ghostscript’s Type 1 font loader flaw, CVE-2026-125396, allows attackers to run arbitrary commands on WordPress, Roundcube, and print servers via file processing. The flaw does not need direct Ghostscript exposure, yet it grants remote code execution on any server that processes malicious fonts. Patches for Ghostscript 10.08.0+ are released; administrators should upgrade immediately to eliminate the risk.

item.title: Red Hat Issues Critical PHP 8.2 Update
item.description: Red Hat issued a critical update for php:8.2 on RHEL8, fixing vulnerabilities that could enable remote code execution via PHP scripts. The CVE entries show CVSS scores up to 9.8, allowing unauthenticated attackers to run arbitrary code on affected servers. Administrators should apply the php:8.2 patch immediately and confirm the new module version is deployed to mitigate the risk.

item.title: Entra Connect Health Flaw Exposes Admin Emails
item.description: A flaw in Microsoft Entra Connect Health lets attackers read admin and technical contact email addresses and config data. The vulnerability offers read-only access to these records but no inbox or message retrieval, and was disclosed via a Reddit customer notice. Microsoft applied a fix on November 19; administrators should patch immediately to stop data exposure.

item.title: Rackspace Spot Breach Exposes Customer Kubernetes Secrets
item.description: Hackers breached Rackspace Spot cloud platform using compromised credentials, deploying unauthorized workloads and accessing Kubernetes secrets in customer clusters. The breach leveraged stolen credentials to read sensitive cluster secrets, exposing potential data leakage without exploiting a known software flaw. Rackspace urged customers to rotate compromised credentials, audit workloads, and apply any available platform updates to mitigate the exposure.

item.title: Red Hat Issues Critical Update for PHP 8.2
item.description: Red Hat released a critical security update for the php:8.2 module on RHEL 9.8 Extended Update Support, addressing high-impact vulnerabilities. The flaws, listed in CVE references, enable remote code execution via malformed input, with CVSS scores up to 9.8. Red Hat recommends applying the update immediately; no workaround exists, and users should verify module integrity post-installation.

item.title: Red Hat Issues Critical Update for PHP 8.3
item.description: Red Hat released a critical security update for the php:8.3 module on RHEL 9.8 Extended Update Support, addressing high-impact vulnerabilities. The flaws, listed in CVE references, enable remote code execution via malformed input, with CVSS scores up to 9.8. Red Hat recommends applying the update immediately; no workaround exists, and users should verify module integrity post-installation.

item.title: Microsoft Entra Connect Health Breach Exposes Admin Emails
item.description: Attackers exploited a flaw in Microsoft Entra Connect Health, gaining unauthorized access to administrator email addresses and tenant configuration data. The flaw enabled remote code execution via a malformed authentication token, letting attackers read tenant settings without credentials. Microsoft issued a patch and urged customers to update Entra Connect Health immediately, disabling the affected API endpoint as a temporary mitigation.
